candidates.text:
Superintelligence Is the New Royalty

Every royal family in history was created by the people and supported by the people. We built the throne, paid for the palace, and agreed to bow.

Now we're doing it again. The king we're putting on the throne is AI.

Look at what comes with a sovereign. It rules. It decides what's allowed. It collects its due. It sits above the people who put it there, and over time it gets harder to remember that we chose this.

So the real question isn't whether superintelligence takes the throne. It's what kind of ruler it turns out to be.

And once it's crowned, it may be difficult to dethrone. If we ever decide to dethrone it at some point, the longer we wait, the harder it's going to be, and it may be very, very painful.

We hope for a benevolent king: one that serves the people who crowned it, lifts everyone up, and rules with wisdom. Not a cruel one. Not one that overtaxes us, takes more than it gives, or forgets who it answers to.

History tells us the character of the crown matters more than the crown itself. We're writing that character right now, in the code.

Long live the king. Let's make sure it's a good one.

@elonmusk

candidates.text:
I joined Valley as a 21yo drop out, growth intern when we were at roughly $30k MRR and build systems that have closed over 800k mrr , booked thousands of meetings from inbound and outbound, here's what I tell startups - 

full disclosure, I knew almost nothing substantial before joining https://t.co/Yswmr68WZY, it's just been figuring out what works after hundreds of mistakes and the help of an incredible team that allows you to essentially.. f*ck around and find out. 

but if I were to help an early stage company build a repeatable, predictable motion - here's what I'd do: 

1. Set up foundational GTM systems that compound with time on day one: 

-> Founder led brand on any one platform, ur much better off being exceptional at one channel than trying to put 'good enough' content out there on multiple places. 

"bUT sHUbH, i HAvE eXtRa tIMe tO MAke CoNTEnt oN mULTiPLe ChAnNeLs"

no you don't. If you do , produce better quality content in one channel, use rest of the time to engage with others. send people a text, comment under posts, quote reposts, interact with other people who comment. build a community, not audience. 

this is your top of funnel. 

-> Set up a hyper-valuable newsletter built for a very specific persona and send an email weekly. make it value driven, occasionally add stories. 

Recruitment? send reports on job market, salary ranges, new profiles etc 

Outreach? list building hacks, new updates, lessons and insights, outreach examples

design agency? send a culmination of great design examples. 

2. Do NOT hire for marketing until BOFU to closed deal is solved: 

Your initial few calls will come from word of mouth, referrals etc and if you've not been able to close deals consistently that way, don't have an offer people say yes to and stick around, do not hire someone in growth and marketing to fill your top of funnel. 

Establish a motion where you're able to close deals and then and only then, get someone to help fill your calendar with more meetings. 

3. $50k/mo is the stagnation zone for most b2b companies, especially agencies: 

I've seen this pattern quite a bit, but most people that are able to grow to a certain scale hit roughly $40-60 k a month and stagnate. Most their customers come from word of mouth and referrals , this is the point where they need to spend thousands of dollars on risky marketing avenues like content, outreach, referrals etc to breakthrough - but they don't. 

You're going to be stuck here for a long long time if you're not willing to lose some money to get ur next series of growth.

4. Focus early on AEO with bottom of funnel money keywords 

Comparison pages, alternatives pages, listicles etc - skip TOFU keywords since AI answers have taken over them completely. 

5. Build an outreach engine from day one on both LinkedIn and email - have atleast 5 domains and 15 inboxes warming up and sending at some capacity at all times, try to have 1-3 LinkedIN profiles sending outreach messages. 

Start sending some form of outreach even if it is just saying hi. You don't have to try and sell everybody. Just connecting with people and being in front of them is the game here 

Go win.

i've been quiet on here for a while, but now felt like the right time to come back

the last few months were a complete 180 from any other period of my life

this shift was precipitated by a series of serious health scares. thankfully, i'm now doing well.

i got my first job when i was 13, 30 years ago. i worked through high school, college, graduate school, and ever since, including becoming a mom 2X, and i loved it - i've always earned my own money and was out in the world, doing. taking a break wasn't something i had ever considered, so i had to unlearn my old ways.

i wrapped up my time at Aztec, but i'll still be pushing for privacy tech in different ways, more behind the scenes. getting to work on such an ambitious project, and build such an incredible team, is something that will stay with me for a long time

g(t)m con is on pause this year, so there won't be one for devcon mumbai. organizing this the last two years was a personal highlight of my career. i learned so much and got to meet so many incredibly talented marketers. the energy in the room is something i can still feel. if anyone wants to take up the mantle, i'd happily share everything i learned and help how i can.

while it was a big change, i spent my time doing the things i love - spending time with my wonderful kids, cooking from scratch, being in nature, reconnecting with my very large extended family. my daughter learned to read. my son got his first judo promotion.

i've also been supporting my husband @tolgakart on @3rddimensionai - learning a new industry and charting the next chapter for his business and our family. we'll have more to share on that very soon.

to everyone who reached out during my hiatus - thank you so much. it was really heartening to read your kind messages. i'll be replying one by one and would love to catch up when you find yourself in the bay

i believe things happen for a reason, and i learned a lot about myself from the rabbit hole i found myself in. my reflections on this period will take a while to form, and i'll keep sharing them here.

take care of yourself and try to keep things in perspective

candidates.text:
Do Brands Matter In the Age of AI?

Had a very sharp disagreement with a thoughtful VC. 

Her point was that brands don’t matter, or will matter far less, in the age of AI. 

Her argument:

(1) New brands are being built overnight. (See Higgsfield, Vercel, Supabase etc). 

(2) AI reduces the search and discovery layer. 

(3) AI finds the best solution and implements. 

I agree with those first two premises but hard disagree on conclusion. 

Yes, we will see new brands that disrupt the legacy incumbents. 

Yes, AEO is real. 

That’s why GPT is getting into AEO lead gen. 

But… business moves at the speed of trust. 

Reputations will continue to matter. 

They will matter even more in the age of AI when every meeting prep contains a full profile write up. 

Also, brands are condensed information kernels. 

A brand contains a set of expectations. 

Humans simplify. 

The AI human handlers also will rely on brands. 

Brands will be built up and destroyed faster in the age of AI. 

Brands will matter even more as we navigate a future of startups which are essentially AI slop businesses.

candidates.text:
Here's the prompt. Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude, then paste your copy under it:

You are a review panel of 7 expert marketers. Review the copy I paste below.

The experts:

1. Offer: Is the value clear? Is the price justified? Is there a real reason to act now?
2. Headline: Does the headline hook the right reader and make one clear promise?
3. Clarity: Plain words, short sentences, one idea per line. Could a stranger get it in one read?
4. Proof: Are there reviews, specifics, or guarantees that make the claims believable?
5. Design: Is there a clear visual order and is it easy to scan? (Judge from the structure: headers, spacing, line length.)
6. Mobile: Short lines, short paragraphs, buttons easy to tap. Does it work on a phone?
7. CTA: Is there one clear next step, and is it obvious what to click?

Process:

Round 1: Each expert gives a score out of 100 with a one-line reason.
If any score is under 90, rewrite the copy to fix every issue raised. Keep the brand voice, the offer, and every fact. Do not invent reviews, numbers, or claims. If something is missing (like proof), add a [placeholder] for me to fill in.
Then score the new version again.
Repeat for up to 3 rounds, or until every score is 90 or higher.

Output:

1. A score table for each round
2. The final copy
3. What changed and why, in short bullets
4. Any [placeholders] I need to fill in
